newsitem.title: USA: Sun Intl gets interim okay in N.J. deal.
newsitem.headline: Sun Intl gets interim okay in N.J. deal.

text.p: Bahamas-based Sun International Hotels Ltd said on Wednesday that the New Jersey Casino Control Commission has approved the company's bid for interim casino authorization, as part of its merger agreement with Griffin Gaming & Entertainment Inc.

The approval lets the $210 million deal proceed, while the New Jersey gaming authorities conduct a routine investigation of Sun International, a spokesman for the New Jersey Casino Control Commission said. The investigation is expected to be completed by spring 1997, officials told Sun.

Sun International said this approval allows the acquisition of Griffin Gaming and its Resorts casino in Atlantic City to proceed ahead of schedule. A vote on the deal by shareholders of both company's is set for December 10, 1996.
Former New Jersey Governor Thomas Kean serves as trustee for all of Griffin Gaming's stock until Sun gets a license, Sun International said.

New Jersey law requires an investigation for any company seeking a license to run a casino. Investigators check the financial stability of the applicant and the character of the people running the business, the Casino Control Commission spokesman said.
